sentence_stem: If I had known about the delay,
correct_completion: I would have taken an earlier train.
full_sentence: If I had known about the delay, I would have taken an earlier train.
acceptable_variants: I would have left the house sooner.
I would have caught an earlier bus.

options.text: I take an earlier train every day.
options.why_wrong: The present simple describes a habit, but the stem sets up an unreal past situation that needs a past conditional result.

options.text: I will take an earlier train tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The future tense refers to a real future plan, which does not match the hypothetical past introduced by 'had known'.

options.text: I would have taken an earlier train.
I would take an earlier train now.
options.why_wrong: This conditional refers to the present, while the 'had known' clause refers to a past situation that did not happen.

grammar_focus: Third conditional (unreal past): if + past perfect, would have + past participle
explanation: After 'if' with the past perfect, the main clause needs 'would have' plus a past participle to show what would have happened. Speakers whose first language has a single conditional form often use a simple conditional here, but English separates the unreal past result from the unreal present result.
translation: Si hubiera sabido del retraso, habría tomado un tren más temprano.
